angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,175,733 km at 413.00 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 2.4213 +/- 0.0166 mas (same row, RUWE 0.87): 413.00 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.69 +/- 0.019 solar radii from Leonardi et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-12 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...686A..84L/abstract): 1,175,733 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.325 +/- 0.026 solar masses from Leonardi et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-12 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...686A..84L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6265 +/- 50 K from Leonardi et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-12 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...686A..84L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Leonardi et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-12 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...686A..84L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-12.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.105, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
